steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dance structure is how a piece is organised — the overall shape and order of sections

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Binary form has two contrasting sections: A then B (e.g. fast then slow)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ternary form has three sections: ABA — the opening section returns after a contrast

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Rondo form alternates a main theme with different episodes: ABACADA

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between binary and ternary form? | Q: Describe the structure of a rondo and give its pattern. | Q: How does an abstract structure differ from a narrative structure?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Binary form has two sections (A B), while ternary form has three (A B A) where the opening section returns after the contrast. | A rondo has a main theme that keeps returning, alternating with different contrasting episodes, following the pattern ABACADA. | A narrative structure tells a story with characters and events in order; an abstract structure is organised around movement ideas and qualities without a storyline.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use the correct letter patterns (AB, ABA, ABACADA) when describing structures Always explain why a choreographer chose that structure — link it to intention In NEA written tasks, name your structure and justify how it supports your idea For professional works, identify the structure and explain how it shapes the audience experience Remember that structure and form are used interchangeably in AQA 8236
